newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's new foreign investment $58.6 mln in Nov.
newsitem.headline: Peru's new foreign investment $58.6 mln in Nov.

text.p: Direct foreign investment in Peru rose $58.6 million in November to a total registered stock of $6.239 billion, the government's National Commission of Foreign Investment and Tecnology (CONITE) said Wednesday.
The CONITE, which could not give comparative figures for November 1995, started registering foreign investment in 1988.
The main investor in Peru in recent years is Spain with $2.37 billion of the total stock. This is due mainly to purchases in local privatizations by Telefonica de Espana and Banco Bilbao Vizcaya.

Other major investors in Peru are the United Kingdom and the United States, which each have a registered stock of $1.09 billion of the total. The next highest investor is the Netherlands with $341.7 million, followed by Panama with $223.2 million, and Chile with $220.2 million.
